newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Arboyne says Nonoc mainly equity funds.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Arboyne says Nonoc mainly equity funds.

text.p: Mining junior Arboyne NL said on Friday the majority of funding for its planned US$370 milliion Philippine nickel project would come from a share placement, with debt playing a more moderate role.
Arboyne said on Thursday it had appointed ING Barings as global co-ordinator and bookrunner for the placement.
McIntosh Corporate Ltd had been appointed lead manager for the Australian component and joint-lead manager for the international component of the capital raising.
Arboyne plans to reopen the long idle Nonoc nickel refining complex, which was one of the world's 10 biggest nickel refineries before closing in 1986.
The complex, capable of producing 65 million pounds of metal a year, was plagued by low metal prices, high energy costs, a devalued Philippine peso and high interest rates.
Arboyne managing director Alan Van Noort told Reuters the final debt/equity mix would be decided in the next few months, with the issue scheduled for the first quarter of next year.
"The brokers have now been appointed. We are in advanced negotiations with lead bankers and once that has been finalised a consensus will be reached," he said.
Funding also depended on a scoping study, due to be completed within a month, which would give a firm idea of the project's cost.
Van Noort said a due diligence study earlier this year estimated replacement value of the plant at US$1-US$1.5 billion.

Arboyne's entry to the project is through its option to buy Pacific Holdings Ltd, a company that acquired Philinco Mining and Industrial Corp, which has concluded an agreement with the Philippines government for the purchase of Nonoc.
